name: Thieboudienne
summary: Senegal's national dish of herb-stuffed fish and vegetables simmered in tomato broth, with the rice cooked in the same pot.
story: Thieboudienne, or ceebu jën in Wolof, is widely regarded as Senegal's national dish and is made for family lunches and special occasions. It is traditionally served on a large communal platter, with the crispy rice at the bottom, called xoñ, prized by many.

items.name: firm white fish steaks
items.note: grouper, snapper or sea bass, cut thick

steps.title: Make the stuffing
steps.text: Pound or blend the parsley, garlic, scotch bonnet, onion, stock cube, salt and pepper into a coarse green paste. Cut deep slits in the fish and press the paste in, saving a spoonful.

steps.title: Fry the fish
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pot and fry the stuffed fish for 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Lift out gently and set aside; the fish is not fully cooked yet.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: In the same oil, fry the onions for 5 minutes. Add tomato paste and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and the oil separates. Add blended tomatoes and the spare paste and cook 5 more minutes.

steps.title: Add water and vegetables
steps.text: Pour in the water, add the dried fish and bring to a boil. Add cassava and carrots first and simmer for 15 minutes, then add cabbage, aubergine and a whole scotch bonnet for another 10-15 minutes until all are tender.

steps.title: Cook the fish
steps.text: Return the fish to the broth and simmer 8-10 minutes until the flesh flakes. Lift fish and vegetables onto a dish and keep warm.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Measure out the broth: use about 5 cups, topped up with water if short. Stir the rinsed rice into it, bring to a boil, cover and cook on lowest heat for 20-25 minutes until the grains are tender and have absorbed the red broth.

steps.title: Crisp the bottom
steps.text: Keep the heat low for the last 5 minutes so a golden, crunchy layer, the xoñ, forms on the base. The rice is ready when it smells toasty and releases from the pot.

steps.title: Serve on a platter
steps.text: Mound the rice on a big platter, arrange fish and vegetables on top and serve with lime and any pepper sauce left.

tips: Pat the fish very dry before frying to prevent splattering.
Do not stir the rice once covered; steam does the work.
Season the broth strongly because the rice absorbs it.
Save the crispy bottom rice for guests; it is a prized part.

swaps.swap: Use a teaspoon of fish sauce or tamarind paste for a salty-sour depth.
Sweet potato or yam are good substitutes, but add them later as they cook faster.
